qualification: The launcher's internal __launcher_snapshot_sha__ marker guard checks only that a string of length 64 was supplied. That marker alone is NOT an authentication mechanism and can be forged by arbitrary caller code. The guard test named unverified_caller_rejected exercises only the ABSENT-marker case, not a forged 64-character marker.
actual_run_binding: The observed v3 run's separate inline caller actually read launcher bytes, computed SHA-256, compared it to the fixed expected dc5f...697e, and passed those SAME bytes to compile; the exact observed command is reproduced in frontier-20261028-d4-reverse-entrypoint-snapshot-v3-proof-v1.md SHA 55cb4fe7ed7a950a8c78e6209d5ead4cfa7bbf3bf41efd02afb55da516753926. The launcher then snapshot-verified the v2 program, and v2 snapshot-verified its helpers/data. Thus the run-specific binding depends on that observed caller and honest shell/Python/hash/OS, not on the marker alone.
limits: No claim of compromised actual run, source falsity or validation failure; no external attestation, untrusted-caller security guarantee, physical theorem, independent family/human/Lean or parent/f62 acceptance. Source/CRT and prior cadence/loader gaps retain their earlier explicit qualifications.
